name: Qiushi Skill

hlido_opinion.headline: A structured methodology pack that gives an AI agent a disciplined way to analyse a problem before acting — genuinely well organised, openly sourced to its texts, and inseparable from the political corpus it is built on.
hlido_opinion.body: The diagnosis this project opens with is sharper than most agent tooling manages: models can now execute, so what separates them is no longer parameter count but whether they have a reliable method for facing a messy problem. It then names five concrete failure modes that anyone who has watched an agent work will recognise — grabbing at everything without identifying what actually matters, answering before investigating, never checking its own output, stopping at the first obstacle, and doing ten things at once badly. That is an accurate list, and the structure offered against it is coherent rather than a bag of tips: one governing principle (start from what objectively exists; let facts set the judgement) over three layers — a philosophical base (contradiction analysis, practice-based epistemology), working methods (investigation, mass line, criticism and self-criticism), and strategy and tactics (protracted strategy, concentration of force, spark-to-prairie-fire, overall coordination). Each of the nine tools carries a core principle, a named source text and an applicable scenario, which is more rigour about provenance than most prompt packs show, and there is a public examples section plus GitHub Discussions for community cases. What a buyer must weigh openly: the nine tools are drawn from Mao Zedong's writings, and the site's framing is explicitly ideological, opening with a revolutionary slogan. That is not hidden — it is the stated premise — but it means adopting this pack imports a particular political vocabulary into an agent's reasoning, which may be unwelcome or unusable in many organisational contexts regardless of how well the underlying heuristics work. Separately, and on this register's own terms: there is no evidence that the methodology improves agent output. No benchmark, no before-and-after, no evaluation. The claim that this makes agents reason better is argued, not measured. The surface is also Chinese-only, with no English documentation captured.

tier_rationale: FADING (61) because the pack is well structured, honest about its sources and addresses a real weakness in agent reasoning, but offers no evidence at all that it improves output — no benchmark, no evaluation, no before-and-after — and its political framing and Chinese-only surface sharply narrow where it can be adopted. Published evaluation against an unaided baseline would move it up; the framing is a buyer's judgement, not a defect.
what_it_does_well: Names a real and under-addressed gap: agents that can execute but have no reliable method for deciding what matters first
Diagnoses five concrete agent failure modes that are recognisable from practice rather than invented for the page
Offers a genuinely structured system — one governing principle over three layers of nine tools — rather than a list of prompt tricks
Every tool cites its source text and states where it applies, which is unusual provenance discipline for a prompt pack
Carries real community examples and an open GitHub Discussions channel rather than only vendor copy
Is open about its ideological basis rather than laundering it into neutral-sounding language
what_it_fails_at: No evidence whatsoever that the methodology improves agent output — no benchmark, evaluation or before-and-after comparison
The surface is Chinese-only; no English documentation was captured, which limits who can adopt it
The political framing (an explicitly revolutionary register, Mao-derived sources) will make the pack unusable in many organisational contexts whatever the heuristics' merit
No installation, packaging or integration path is visible on the captured page — it is unclear how an agent actually loads this
No versioning, maintenance cadence or licence stated on the reviewed surface
best_for: Chinese-reading practitioners who want a structured reasoning discipline layered onto an agent rather than ad-hoc prompting
Anyone studying how to encode an explicit analytical method into agent behaviour, as a design reference
Users comfortable with the source corpus and the framing it brings
not_recommended_for: Organisations that need politically neutral tooling, or that cannot import this vocabulary into their systems
Buyers who need evidence that a methodology pack measurably improves output before adopting it
Non-Chinese-reading users — there is no English surface captured
Teams needing a packaged, versioned, licensed artifact with a clear install path
red_flags: The core claim — that this methodology makes an agent reason better — is argued at length and never measured; no benchmark or evaluation appears anywhere on the surface

The pack encodes an explicitly political corpus into an agent's reasoning layer; this is stated openly, but buyers should treat it as a deliberate choice with organisational consequences, not a neutral technique
No licence, version or install path is stated for something meant to be loaded into an agent

compared_to.verdict_diff: smol-ai is executable agent tooling with code behind it; Qiushi Skill is a reasoning methodology with no runtime of its own. They are complements rather than alternatives — one runs, the other prescribes how to think.

Claude Code is a complete agent harness that ships its own working discipline; Qiushi Skill is a prompt-layer methodology you would load into such a harness. One is the vehicle, the other a proposed driving style.
